newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Beobanka to woo savings with Greek help.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Beobanka to woo savings with Greek help.

text.p: Yugoslavia's largest commercial bank Beobanka said on Thursday it planned to attract more individual saving deposits by entering a deal with a Greek bank.
"We plan to sign a cooperation agreement with Greek IBG agricultural bank, probably some time next week in Athens," Beobanka spokesman Zoran Pavlovic told Reuters.
The deal envisages IBG as a guarantor for new Yugoslav savings, he said.
Economists see fresh savings as key to reviving the troubled and oversized banking sector, buckling under the burden of huge external and internal debt.
Yugoslavs lost trust in local banks after the government froze 6.6 billion German marks in old hard currency savings.

Since 1993 hyperinflation -- running at 60 percent a day -- there have been practically no fresh savings. According to some estimates, Yugoslavs keep at least three billion German marks "under their mattresses".
"Beobanka hopes the deal with the Greek bank will help woo a great deal of money back to banks," Pavlovic said.
According to Pavlovic, Beobanka is negotiating similar deals with a group of German, British and French banks.
